title: HDFC Bank board 'successfully resolves' issues, submits names for CEO and MD’s job to RBI: Source- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: The board under chairman Rajiv Kumar has moved to stabilise HDFC Bank following the abrupt exit of former chairman Atanu Chakraborty and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s decision not to seek reappointment   September 12, 2026 / 21:25 IST             The board of HDFC Bank has “successfully” completed the operation of “resolving” the issues that had plagued the bank since the abrupt resignation of former chairman Atanu Chakraborty, and a new chief executive will be in place “very soon,” a person aware of the developments said. HDFC Bank’s board on Saturday approved the appointment process for the bank’s Managing Director and CEO and submitted names of two candidates to the RBI for its approval. Several names have been doing the rounds, including internal candidates from the bank as well as external ones. “Within one and a half months, the board has undertaken several steps to shore up confidence in the bank. The clean-up act began soon after the new part-time chairman took over,” the person said on condition of anonymity. He pointed to the number of steps, which began with the “honourable exit” provided to incumbent CEO Sasidhar Jagdishan, who is set to retire on October 26. HDFC also won all seven cases that some investors in Bahrain filed, linked to the Credit Suisse AT1 bond issues, providing much-needed relief to the embattled bank. Clean up act, better succession planning “There is nothing fundamentally wrong with the bank. It is a very strong entity. Had the board led by the new chairman not acted swiftly there could have been more trouble for the bank. It is a very important bank and the steps taken have helped stabilise the situation,” the person said, adding that the selection of two names for the CEO and MD’s post and other announcements unveiled on Saturday had “more or less completed the clean-up act.” He said the move to create an additional post of a whole-time director and increase the number of whole-time directors on the board of the bank to four in addition to the MD and CEO was meant to have “ better succession planning” and ensure there is a strong talent pool. The Reserve Bank of India, the sector’s regulator, approves top-level banking appointments. A source had earlier told Moneycontrol on August 31 that a new CEO at HDFC Bank would be appointed “well before” October 26 and the Board was likely to back a candidate with strong leadership qualities who can take the bank to the “top level”. The board under chairman Rajiv Kumar has moved to stabilise HDFC Bank following the abrupt exit of former chairman Atanu Chakraborty and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s decision not to seek reappointment

September 12, 2026 / 21:25 IST

The board of HDFC Bank has “successfully” completed the operation of “resolving” the issues that had plagued the bank since the abrupt resignation of former chairman Atanu Chakraborty, and a new chief executive will be in place “very soon,” a person aware of the developments said.

HDFC Bank’s board on Saturday approved the appointment process for the bank’s Managing Director and CEO and submitted names of two candidates to the RBI for its approval. Several names have been doing the rounds, including internal candidates from the bank as well as external ones.

“Within one and a half months, the board has undertaken several steps to shore up confidence in the bank. The clean-up act began soon after the new part-time chairman took over,” the person said on condition of anonymity.

He pointed to the number of steps, which began with the “honourable exit” provided to incumbent CEO Sasidhar Jagdishan, who is set to retire on October 26.

HDFC also won all seven cases that some investors in Bahrain filed, linked to the Credit Suisse AT1 bond issues, providing much-needed relief to the embattled bank.

Clean up act, better succession planning

“There is nothing fundamentally wrong with the bank. It is a very strong entity. Had the board led by the new chairman not acted swiftly there could have been more trouble for the bank. It is a very important bank and the steps taken have helped stabilise the situation,” the person said, adding that the selection of two names for the CEO and MD’s post and other announcements unveiled on Saturday had “more or less completed the clean-up act.”

He said the move to create an additional post of a whole-time director and increase the number of whole-time directors on the board of the bank to four in addition to the MD and CEO was meant to have “ better succession planning” and ensure there is a strong talent pool.

The Reserve Bank of India, the sector’s regulator, approves top-level banking appointments. A source had earlier told Moneycontrol on August 31 that a new CEO at HDFC Bank would be appointed “well before” October 26 and the Board was likely to back a candidate with strong leadership qualities who can take the bank to the “top level”.
